title: observability: token-level KV cost/latency dashboard + alert tuning
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds token-level KV metrics and a new observability dashboard to help SREs and runtime engineers understand per-token cost and latency contributions from KV cache interactions. Includes alert tuning to reduce noisy pages and a rollout canary plan.
description:
Motivation: We need better visibility into how KV cache behavior affects per-token cost and latency across workloads. Current dashboards surface per-request metrics but hide token-level effects (prefix cache hits/misses, incremental token latency, and cost attribution), which makes it hard to diagnose regressions and tune batching/caching policies.

Summary: This PR adds a token-level KV metrics pipeline, Grafana dashboard JSON, and tuned alert rules. New metrics include token_kv_cache_hit_rate, token_kv_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), token_cost_per_token_usd, and token_kv_miss_count aggregated by model, route, and customer_tier. The dashboard exposes per-route token cost breakdown, KV cache hit/miss heatmaps, and a latency waterfall visualizing KV lookup time vs model decode time.

Changes: - telemetry/metrics/token_kv_ingest.py: new aggregation job that converts raw traces into token-level metrics with labels (model, route, tier). - telemetry/schema/token_metrics_v2.proto: schema additions for token dimensions. - observability/dashboards/token_kv_cost_latency.json: Grafana dashboard with panels for cost, latency, and cache heatmaps. - observability/alerts/token_kv_alerts.yaml: tuned alerts (thresholds, MUTE windows, staging vs prod thresholds). - docs/observability/token_kv_dashboard.md: how-to and runbook for alerts and common mitigations. - tests/telemetry/test_token_aggregation.py: unit tests for aggregation logic.

Testing: Unit tests cover the aggregation logic and label propagation. Integration run executed against staging traces (sample of 1M tokens) and validated that new metrics match the golden reference within 0.5% for counts. Dashboard panels were smoke-tested in staging with canary traffic. CI initially failed on a flake in integration-tests, re-ran and passed.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge and deploy metrics ingestion to staging. 2) Deploy dashboard + alerts to staging and run 48h canary with canary flag enabled for 10% of production traffic. 3) If no regressions and acceptable alert noise reduction, deploy to prod. Alerts include two tuning steps: soft-alerts at higher thresholds for 72h, then reduce to aggressive thresholds if stable. Runbook: docs/observability/token_kv_dashboard.md includes steps to mute/unmute and investigate spike sources.

Related: Linked Linear tickets ENG-1842 (token-level observability initiative) and SRE-47 (alert noise reduction). Support ticket SUP-893 reported customer-facing latency regressions that motivated alert thresholds for low-tier customers.

Notes: This PR is focused on observability and does not change runtime behavior. Future follow-ups will surface adaptive cache recommendations in Redwood Optimize and support rollouts for per-customer thresholds.
